text: A survey shows that 73% of the persons working in an office like coffee, whereas 65% like tea. If x denotes the percentage of them, who like both coffee and tea, then x cannot be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
C $\to$ person like coffee

T $\to$ person like Tea

n(C) = 73

n(T) = 65

n(C $\cup$ T) $\leq$ 100

n(C) + n(T) – n (C $\cap$ T) $\leq$ 100

73 + 65 – x $\leq$ 100

x $\geq$ 38

73 – x $\geq$ 0 $\Rightarrow$ x $\leq$ 73

65 – x $\geq$ 0 $\Rightarrow$ x $\leq$ 65

$\therefore$ 38 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 65
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
If $3^{2\sin 2α-1}$, 14 and $3^{4-2\sin 2α}$ are the first three terms of an A.P. for some $α$, then the sixth
term of this A.P. is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that

$3^{4-2\sin 2α}+3^{2\sin 2α-1}=28$

Let $3^{2\sin 2α}$ = t

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{81}{t}+\frac{t}{3}=28$

$\Rightarrow$t = 81, 3

$\therefore$ $3^{2\sin 2α}$ $= 3^{1}, 3^{4}$

$\sin 2α=\frac{1}{2}$, 2 (rejected)

First term a = $3^{2\sin 2α-1}$ $= 3^{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ a = 1

Given Second term = 14

$\therefore$ Common difference d = 13

$T_{6}=a+5d$

$T_{6}=1+5\times 13$

$T_{6}=66$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
Let $λ\in$ R . The system of linear equations

$2x_{1}$
$- 4x_{2} +$ $λx_{3} = 1$

$x_{1} - 6x_{2} + x_{3} = 2$

$λx_{1} - 10x_{2} + 4x_{3} = 3$

is inconsistent for:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
D = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -4 & λ \\ 1 & -6 & 1 \\ λ & -10 & 4 \end{array}\right |$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 3, $-\frac{2}{3}$

$D_{1} =$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & -4 & λ \\ 2 & -6 & 1 \\ 3 & -10 & 4 \end{array}\right |$

= 14 + 4(5) + $λ$(–2)

= –2$λ$ + 6

$D_{2} =$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 1 & λ \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ λ & 3 & 4 \end{array}\right |$

= –2($λ$ – 3)($λ$ + 1)

$D_{3} =$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -6 & 2 \\ λ & -10 & 3 \end{array}\right |$

= – 2$λ$ + 6

When , $λ$ = 3 then

$D = D_{1} = D_{2} = D_{3} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ Infinite many solution

When $λ$ = $-\frac{2}{3}$ then $D_{1}, D_{2}, D_{3}$ none of them is zero so equations are inconsistant.

$\therefore$ $λ$ = $-\frac{2}{3}$

text:
If the point P on the curve, $4x^{2} + 5y^{2} = 20$ is 
farthest from the point Q(0, -4), then $PQ^{2}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given ellipse is $\frac{x^{2}}{5}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1$

Let point P is $(\sqrt{5}\cos θ,2\sin θ)$

$(PQ)^{2}=5\cos ^{2}θ+(2\sin θ+4)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(PQ)^{2} =$ $5\cos ^{2}θ+4\sin ^{2}θ+16\sin θ+16$

$\Rightarrow$ $(PQ)^{2} =$ $\cos ^{2}θ+4\cos ^{2}θ+4\sin ^{2}θ+16\sin θ+16$

$\Rightarrow$ $(PQ)^{2} =$ $\cos ^{2}θ+4+16\sin θ+16$

$\Rightarrow$ $(PQ)^{2}=\cos ^{2}θ+16\sin θ+20$

$\Rightarrow$ $(PQ)^{2}=-\sin ^{2}θ+16\sin θ+21$

= $-\left (\sin ^{2}θ-2.8\sin θ+64\right )+64+21$

= $85-(\sin θ-8)^{2}$

will be maximum when sin $θ$ = 1

$\Rightarrow (PQ)^{2}_{\max }=85-49=36$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
The product of the roots of the 
equation $9x^{2} - 18|x| + 5 = 0$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$9x^{2}-18|x|+5=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $9x^{2}-15|x|-3|x|+5=0$ ($\because$ $x^{2} =$ $|x|^{2}$)

$\Rightarrow$ $3|x|(3|x|-5)-(3|x|-5)=0$

$\Rightarrow|x|=\frac{1}{3},\frac{5}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\pm \frac{1}{3},\pm \frac{5}{3}$

$\therefore$ Product of roots 

= $\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )\left (-\frac{1}{3}\right )\left (\frac{5}{3}\right )\left (-\frac{5}{3}\right )$
= $\frac{25}{81}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
If the function 
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} k_{1}(x-π)^{2}-1, & x\leq π \\ k_{2}\cos x, & x>π \end{array} \right.$  is
 twice differentiable, then the ordered pair $(k_{1}, k_{2})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For continuity at $x=π$: $f(π)=k_{1}\cdot 0-1=-1$ and $\lim _{x\to π^{+}}k_{2}\cos x=-k_{2}$, so $k_{2}=1$.

The first derivative is

$f^{'}(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 2k_{1}(x-π), & x<π \\ -k_{2}\sin x, & x>π \end{array} \right.$

Both one-sided values at $x=π$ are 0, so $f^{'}(π)=0$ for all $k_{1},k_{2}$.

The second derivative is

$f^{''}(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} 2k_{1}, & x<π \\ -k_{2}\cos x, & x>π \end{array} \right.$

For $f^{''}(π)$ to exist, $2k_{1}=-k_{2}\cos π=k_{2}=1$, so $k_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Therefore $(k_{1},k_{2})=\left (\dfrac{1}{2},1\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
If 
$\int \left (e^{2x}+2e^{x}-e^{-x}-1\right )e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}dx$ = $g(x)e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}+c$

where c is a constant of integration,
then g(0) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
I = $\int \left (e^{2x}+2e^{x}-e^{-x}-1\right )e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}dx$

= $\int \left (\left (e^{2x}+e^{x}-1\right )+(e^{x}-e^{-x})\right )e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}dx$

= $\int \left (e^{2x}+e^{x}-1\right )e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}dx$

+ $\int e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}(e^{x}-e^{-x})dx$

= $\int \frac{\left (e^{2x}+e^{x}-1\right )e^{\left (ex+e-x\right )}}{e^{x}}.e^{x}dx$

$+\int e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}(e^{x}-e^{-x})dx$

= $\int (e^{x}-e^{-x}+1)e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x}+x)}dx$

+ $\int e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}(e^{x}-e^{-x})dx$

Let $e^{x}+e^{-x}+x$ = t $\Rightarrow$ $(e^{x}-e^{-x}+1)$dx = dt

and let $e^{x}+e^{-x}$ = u $\Rightarrow$ $(e^{x}-e^{-x})dx$ = du

$\therefore$ I = $\int e^{t}dt+\int e^{u}du$

= $e^{t}$ + $e^{u}$ + C

= $e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x}+x)}$ + $e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}$ + C

= $e^{(e^{x}+e^{-x})}(e^{x}+1)$ + C

$\therefore$ $g(x) = e^{x} + 1$ 

$\Rightarrow$ g(0) = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text: The number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed by taking 4 letters at a time from the letters of the word ’SYLLABUS’ such that two letters are distinct and two letters are alike, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In 'SYLLABUS' word

1. Two S letters

2. Two L letters

3. One Y letter

4. One A letter

5. One B letter

6. One U letter

Number of ways we can select two alike
letters $= ^{2}C_{1}$

Then number of ways we can select two distinct
letters $= ^{5}C_{2}$

Then total arrangement of
selected letters = $\frac{4!}{2!}$

So total number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed

$= ^{2}C_{1}$ $\times$ $^{5}C_{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{4!}{2!}$ = 240
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
If the line, 2x - y + 3 = 0 is at a distance
 $\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$
and $\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ from the lines 4x - 2y + $α$ = 0 
and 6x - 3y + $β$ = 0, respectively, then the sum of all possible values of $α$ and $β$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Apply distance between parallel line formula

$4x-2y+α=0$

$4x-2y+6=0$

$\left |\frac{α-6}{2\sqrt{5}}\right |=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

$|α-6|=2\Rightarrow α=8,4$

sum = 12

Again 

$6x-3y+β=0$

$6x-3y+9=0$

$\left |\frac{β-9}{3\sqrt{5}}\right |=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$

$|β-9|=6\Rightarrow β=15,3$

sum = 18

$\therefore$ Sum of all values of $α$ and $β$ is = 30
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot
